short: The rule that turns genotypes into numbers: usually the count, 0, 1 or 2, of one chosen allele (the counted allele). Which allele is counted differs between files and programs, so the rule must travel with the numbers.
long:
At a SNP with alleles C and T, counting C codes the genotypes TT, CT and CC as 0, 1 and 2; counting T codes them as 2, 1 and 0. PLINK 1.9 counts its A1 allele (made the minor allele when it writes a fileset), a VCF's dosage counts ALT, and PLINK 2's --export A counts REF by default.

Switching the counted allele replaces each count g by 2 − g, the allele frequency p by 1 − p, a regression slope β by −β (the intercept α by α + 2β), and an odds ratio by its reciprocal; fit statistics and p-values do not change. Other codings exist for other models: dominant coding (1 if at least one copy, else 0) and recessive coding (1 only for two copies).
l1: Page 4 shows which allele each file format counts and lets you switch the counted allele in a small dataset.

links.t: PLINK 2.0: --export A counts REF by default

short: A single-base change between the two purines, A and G, or between the two pyrimidines, C and T. Transitions arise more often than other base changes, so most SNPs are A/G or C/T.
long:
The other base changes, a purine replaced by a pyrimidine or the reverse, are transversions. In the PennCATH array data, 575,207 of the 835,319 SNPs with two alleles (69%) are transitions.

A transition can always be strand-aligned from its letters: the complement of A/G is T/C, a different pair.
l1: Page 4 counts the allele pairs of all PennCATH SNPs.

short: A single-base change from a purine (A or G) to a pyrimidine (C or T) or back: A/C, A/T, G/C or G/T. The A/T and C/G transversions are the SNPs whose letters read the same on both strands.
long: Transversions are less frequent than transitions. In the PennCATH array data, 260,112 of the 835,319 SNPs with two alleles are transversions, and 128,999 of them are A/T or C/G: strand-ambiguous SNPs that can be aligned between files only by their allele frequencies.
